title: Privacy-Preserving Crowd and Traffic Counting
description:
Cities, transport operators and venue managers need numbers about how public spaces are used: how many pedestrians and cyclists pass a street, how full a square or platform is, how much traffic of each vehicle type uses a road. Manual counts are expensive and rare. The goal is a video analytics system that counts people and vehicles automatically and outputs only anonymous, aggregated numbers.

Requirements

  • Count people, bicycles, cars, buses and trucks crossing a line, per direction and time interval.
  • Measure the occupancy of defined zones over time.
  • Run on existing cameras, on a CPU or a small edge device.
  • Deliver counts to a dashboard or database.

Privacy constraints

  • No face recognition, no biometric identification and no tracking of individuals across cameras or over time.
  • Video frames are processed in memory and not stored; only aggregate counts leave the system.
  • Purpose, legal basis and retention are documented (for example in a GDPR data protection impact assessment) and people are informed with signage.
goals:
• Counts within 10 % of a manual count for each camera, checked on at least one hour of footage per camera.
  • No video frames or images of people stored or transmitted; only per-interval counts.
  • Counts available on the dashboard within one aggregation interval (for example one minute).
  • Runs at least 5 processed frames per second per camera on the target hardware.
